findings.title: Control rollback can remove the built-in-account downgrade guard
findings.trigger: After updating trusted control tools and activating built-in accounts or migrating HTTPS, invoke ordinary control-rollback for a committed generation whose capabilities provide system-v1/nativeWorkspace but predate built-in-account support.
findings.impact: The rollback admission checks only provider-layer and workspace compatibility and accepts an account-incompatible retained control generation. This replaces the trusted manager containing require_account_compatibility, leaving the subsequent ordinary application rollback path without the new account downgrade protection; retained account credentials and second-factor policy can consequently be bypassed by an accidental legacy application downgrade. The current staged capabilities also omit any account-guard version, so compatibility cannot be positively distinguished.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit built-in-account/downgrade-guard capability to staged control generations and reject rollback to a generation lacking that capability before stopping or publishing whenever a bootstrap exists, HTTPS uses built-in authentication, or the selected verified release declares account-v1. Cover both bootstrap/edge markers and browser-initialized selected-release detection with targeted transaction regressions; preserve compatible control rollback and failure recovery.
evidence: deploy/control_update.py:386-392 checks providerConfigLayer and nativeWorkspace only.
deploy/install.py:66 emits no built-in-account or authentication-downgrade capability.
deploy/manager.py:98-105 contains the account compatibility guard that control rollback can remove.

.work/v210-audit1-control-rollback-probe.json: the current synthetic control fixture accepted rollback with an auth-bootstrap marker and authentication=builtin; retained capabilities contained only format/providerConfigLayer/nativeWorkspace.
findings.reproductionLimits: Only the current synthetic fixture and opaque placeholder old/new deployment files were used. System/process commands were substituted; no legacy implementation, root systemd, SSH, online instance or actual legacy application was executed.

untestedIntegrations: No full suite was run. Root-owned Linux/systemd, real reboot/cgroup behavior, actual external HTTPS/login, provider services and online deployment were not executed by this reviewer; the parent owns separate isolated directed regression evidence.
method: Independent current-source semantic review of all 80 deployment-domain files: 43 deployment implementation/documentation files and 37 tests/probes. Read full files and reread sections obscured by output truncation. Traced install/update/rollback/repair, root bootstrap/reset and connection-bound HMAC login proof, HTTPS migration and restoration, trusted control update/rollback/recovery, provider/config generations, root/native/control/gateway ownership, exact systemd/cgroup stop evidence, request receipts/spool, candidate isolation/import and resource budgets, workspace descriptor boundaries, recovery/acknowledgements, Git index/ref transactions and managed worktrees. Ran one narrow synthetic control-rollback probe using the current test fixture with substituted system/process operations, recorded its limitations, and did not run any suite or network/SSH action. Recomputed the current complete source snapshot: 1848 files and the assigned digest are unchanged. No source changes were made; all assigned files were inspected. Completion denotes full assigned audit coverage, not a clean result.
